subject: Realtime latency spike affecting Qterra ingestion (us-west-2)
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Khan <samira@qterra.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Realtime latency spike affecting Qterra ingestion (us-west-2)

Hi Samira —

We’re seeing a sustained increase in tail latency for the embeddings endpoint that your ingestion pipeline uses in us-west-2 starting ~07:45 PDT. Symptoms: per-request p95/p99 increased, a small number (~2%) of in-flight requests timed out and were retried, which correlates with the backpressure you reported this morning. Impact: slower ingestion and occasional duplicate events on your side.

Immediate actions we’ve taken:
- Opened an incident (PagerDuty PDR-87421) and assigned to the runtime-oncall team.
- Scaled the GPU pool for the embeddings pool for your tenant by +20% to relieve queueing.
- Rolled a config that reduces max batch size for very short sequences.

As next steps we’ll:
1) Monitor for normalization over the next 30–60 minutes.
2) If tail latency remains elevated, we’ll rollback the recent kernel tuning from last night (v2.1 -> v2.0) and queue a canary.
3) Share customer-facing status updates at 30m cadence until resolved.

I’ve attached recent tail-latency logs and a short screenshot of the queue length. We’ll follow up with an executive summary within 3 hours and a postmortem within 72 hours.

Can you confirm: are you seeing retries/duplicates on your side beyond what you expected? Any live dashboards or traces you can share will help accelerate root cause.

Thanks,
Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Senior Customer Ops Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachments: qterra_tail_latency_logs_20260310.csv, qterra_incident_screenshot.png
From: Samira Khan <samira@qterra.ai>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: Qterra SRE <sre@qterra.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 08:23:45 -07:00
Subject: Re: Realtime latency spike affecting Qterra ingestion (us-west-2)

Thanks Lauren —

We see a corresponding rise in ingestion latency and ~1.8% duplicate events from our retry logic. We didn’t change any client-side settings this morning.

We have a live dashboard URL: https://grafana.qterra.ai/d/ingest and a trace link I added to the shared Drive. Our SREs are standing by on the incident bridge.

Is there an ETA for rollback if scaling doesn’t normalize? We’d prefer the rollback if that brings immediate relief.

—Samira
Samira Khan
Head of Site Reliability, Qterra AI

Hi Samira —

Thanks for the dashboard link and the confirmation. Short update: scaling helped reduce queue depth but we’re still seeing elevated p99 for short sequences. Per runbook we’ve queued the rollback to kernel tuning v2.0 as a canary (impact window <5m) and scheduled it to start at 09:05 PDT if metrics haven’t returned to baseline.

Mitigation summary:
- Scaling: +20% capacity (completed 08:30 PDT).
- Canary rollback scheduled (09:05 PDT).
- Client-side recommendation: increase ingest timeout to 10s and add idempotency keys to avoid duplicates during retries.

I’ve attached the mitigation runbook we followed (mitigation-runbook-v2.pdf). We’ll keep you updated on the canary result and will call if the rollback is required.

If rollback proceeds, we expect a short maintenance window for the embeddings pool (aiming for sub-5 minute impact) and will coordinate exact timing with your SRE team.

Lauren

Attachments: mitigation-runbook-v2.pdf

Subject: Fwd: Realtime latency spike affecting Qterra ingestion — internal exec brief (for leadership)

Team — quick internal note to prep an executive-facing update for Qterra and to capture follow-ups for the postmortem. Please hold for a 09:30 call with Qterra execs (H1 product/ops). I’ll draft the one-paragraph update but need the following from you by 09:00:

- Marcus: an engineer-friendly summary of root cause hypotheses and the expected rollback impact (1–2 bullets).
- Hannah: cost/credits ask if the customer requests goodwill credits for retries or duplicate processing — provide recommended range and precedent.

Current status: scaling reduced queue depth; canary scheduled 09:05 PDT; monitoring for normalization.

We should be prepared to offer a 10% credits gesture if we confirm customer-visible duplication >1% and sustained for >30m. That’s a preliminary number; Hannah please advise.

I’m looping in Leadership once we have canary outcome.

-Lauren

Subject: Qterra update: latency resolved, next steps and postmortem timeline

Hi Samira —

Quick executive update following the rollback canary this morning: we rolled back last-night kernel tuning at 09:05 PDT and observed p99 tail latency return to baseline within ~7 minutes. We kept capacity scaled for the next 45 minutes to drain any queued work and validated success against your ingestion dashboard.

What we did:
- Immediate scale up (+20%) to relieve queueing.
- Canary rollback of kernel tuning (v2.1 -> v2.0) at 09:05 PDT.
- Validation against your Grafana traces and our internal telemetry.

Customer impact: brief increase in ingest latency and ~1.8% duplicate events during the 07:45–09:12 PDT window. We have recommendations to reduce risk going forward:
- We’ll provide a hardened kernel tuning patch and per-tenant canary gating (ETA 4 days).
- Recommend you increase client timeout to 10s and enable idempotency keys for the ingestion path.

Next steps & timeline:
- Postmortem (internal + customer summary) draft shared by Fri, 13 Mar 2026.
- Follow-up call to review postmortem and remediation plan: propose Mon, 16 Mar 2026.
- Ticket opened for long-term mitigation (priority P2): SUP-2891.

We apologize for the disruption. Hannah will follow up with a proposed credit recommendation for the duplicate processing and Marcus will share the technical postmortem outline once we’ve closed telemetry analysis.

If you’d like a single-slide executive summary for your leadership, let me know and we’ll send it within the hour.

Thanks for your patience and for collaborating closely with our oncall.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Senior Customer Ops Manager
Redwood Inference
